data.body:
Phase 1 root cause (cited): shim.py review_code() gated on gate_dispatch.code_review_enabled() (verify.enable_code_review, default False) and returned _disabled_review_result() — so the explicit CLI/library/MCP surface was silently inert. Caller inventory (Serena find_referencing_symbols + grep-as-string): code_review_enabled has exactly two prod callers (the shim + the enabled=None fallback in _code_review_preflight); shim.review_code is reached only from explicit surfaces (CLI _llm_commands.py, MCP _mcp_llm.py, library export); produce_code_review_verdict's only other direct caller is review_bot/adapter.py (already enabled=True).

Fix (per operator ruling, mirroring review-plan's availability-vs-requiredness shape): the shim now always dispatches the gate with enabled=True — an explicit invocation is the caller's intent. verify.enable_code_review keeps its exact current meaning for dispatch-level callers that leave enabled=None (automated paths unchanged; no enforcement added — out of scope). _disabled_review_result and the CLI's dead code-review-disabled exit branch removed. Without the [agents] extra, an explicit run now degrades honestly to INDETERMINATE (library: no raise; CLI: exit 2) instead of a PASS-looking empty result — verified by simulation. RED→GREEN: new test test_review_code_runs_gate_even_when_config_key_is_off seen failing on the old code, green after the fix; disabled-behavior tests repointed at the dispatch level. Docs updated (passing-code-review guide, llm-framework.md, _config_schema comment, package docstrings). make lint, mypy (619 files), complexity ratchet (new=0 increased=0, stale=1 = sanctioned improvement), 200 targeted tests pass.
